title: Integration discovery - Spectra Payments & Redwood
summary: Initial integration discovery focusing on whether Spectra should use Redwood hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Key concerns: latency for payments flows, data residency and encryption (KMS/HSM), integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex stacks, gateway/proxy setup, rate limiting and per-route quotas, and observability hooks for tracing and cost breakdowns.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Rate limits / quotas and burst handling
action_items: Maya Chen: Send Dedicated capacity deck + sample pricing (due 2027-04-01)
Arjun Patel: Share LangChain + LlamaIndex integration examples and a small code snippet for prefix caching (due 2027-03-31)
Lena Rodriguez: Provide expected QPS and 95th percentile latency SLOs (due 2027-03-30)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated capacity options
Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Spectra SREs to run a quick benchmark (estimate 2 weeks)
Customer to share anonymized traffic pattern CSV for batching/quantization recommendations
header:
Date: 2027-03-28
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Rodriguez (Spectra Head of Platform), Tom Wei (SRE), Priya Sharma (ML lead)
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, with Arjun from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Lena Rodriguez: Hey Maya, doing good. Thanks for making time. We're excited to see how Redwood fits with our payments fraud and chat flows.
[00:12] Tom Wei: Hi all, Tom here, SRE. Quick note - we care a lot about latency on the critical payment path, so we'll be asking about p99 and tail behavior.

[00:20] Maya Chen: Totally, that's top of mind. Quick agenda: run through your current stack and constraints, map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, discuss SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations, gateway/proxy patterns, quotas/rate limits, and observability hooks. Then agree next steps.

[00:32] Priya Sharma: Sounds good. For context we run a mix - some in-house transformer models for offline scoring, but online we use an API-based aggregator right now. We're evaluating Redwood because of cost, fallback reliability and private deployment options.
[00:45] Arjun Patel: Got it. When you say API aggregator, is that a custom gateway that fans out to multiple models, or are you using a vendor?

[00:52] Priya Sharma: It's internal - a proxy that routes to open-source models we host. It's getting expensive as traffic grows; we want to see if Redwood hosted or Dedicated pool gives better unit economics and reliability.
[01:05] Lena Rodriguez: Also we need SOC2-level audit logs and KMS integration for keys. Data residency - EU region for European traffic - is a must.

[01:15] Maya Chen: We support region pinning and KMS/HSM integrations on Dedicated and Private. Hosted also supports region routing and we provide audit logs and export hooks - for some customers audit retention is an add-on. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[01:30] Tom Wei: How does the networking look for Private vs Dedicated? We can't open a bunch of ports; we prefer a VPC peering or private link style integration.

[01:38] Arjun Patel: For Private you get a customer-managed control plane and can deploy within your VPC; Dedicated can be set up with private connectivity and IP allowlists, and we support VPC peering / PrivateLink. On Hosted you use TLS over public endpoints but you can restrict by API keys and IP allowlists.
[01:55] Priya Sharma: On the integration side, we use LangChain and LlamaIndex in our pipelines. Are there first-class connectors?

[02:02] Arjun Patel: Yes - we have SDKs in Python/Node and official LangChain adapters plus community LlamaIndex examples. I can drop a repo link and a minimal code snippet showing streaming and embeddings + cache usage.
[02:18] Lena Rodriguez: We rely heavily on streaming for user-facing chat. Our p50 is fine but the p95 needs to be under 300ms for short prompts. Can Hosted meet that or do we need Dedicated?

[02:28] Maya Chen: It's workload-dependent. Hosted often hits sub-300ms for small models and short contexts, but for predictable tail latency Dedicated with reserved GPU capacity is the safer bet. Also Dedicated gives you guaranteed throughput and lower variance.
[02:45] Tom Wei: What about batching and KV cache behavior? Our traffic has a lot of repeated prefixes for templated receipts; we'd like prefix caching so tokens don't get recomputed.

[02:54] Arjun Patel: We provide prefix/KV caching in the runtime. For Hosted there are automatic caching heuristics; Dedicated/Private expose more tunables - you can control cache TTLs and pin large KV cache sizes. That often reduces token cost significantly for templated flows.
[03:12] Priya Sharma: For our team, integrating from LangChain we need to control the request->response path. Can we insert a local gateway or do you recommend calling Redwood endpoints directly?

[03:22] Arjun Patel: Both are common. Customers either call Redwood directly from their app or run a small gateway/proxy that handles auth, rate-limit enforcement, and request enrichment. We have examples of a lightweight sidecar that transparently forwards to Redwood and tracks per-route cost metrics.
[03:38] Lena Rodriguez: About quotas - we want per-route quotas and burst handling. During seasonal spikes we can't have throttles dropping payment verification requests.

[03:46] Maya Chen: Redwood's routing supports per-route quotas and tiered fallback policies. You can set high-priority routes for critical flows that will use Dedicated or warm standby slots; for non-critical flows you can fallback to cheaper model variants or cached responses.
[03:58] Tom Wei: If we do a Dedicated pool and hit capacity, is there an automatic fallback to Hosted?

[04:04] Arjun Patel: Yes, we can configure smart routing: prefer Dedicated but fallback to Hosted or a smaller model variant if Dedicated is saturated. That avoids dropouts but you get predictable degradation.
[04:18] Priya Sharma: On observability, we need per-token cost breakdowns and tracing from our request ID through the model. Does Redwood propagate trace IDs?

[04:25] Maya Chen: We support trace propagation - X-Request-Id and standard OpenTelemetry headers. In the Console you'll see per-route latency and token breakdowns, plus traces linked to request IDs. We can also export to your Datadog/NewRelic instance.
[04:40] Lena Rodriguez: And for security reviews we'll need our legal folks to see SOC 2 reports, encryption details, and a data flow diagram.
[04:47] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC2 and a high-level architecture diagram. For Private deployments we can do an on-prem package for air-gapped setups if that's ever required.
[04:58] Tom Wei: Can you talk about SDK rate limit handling? If our gateway sends bursts, will Redwood queue or reject?

[05:04] Arjun Patel: The SDKs include retry/backoff primitives and client-side rate limiters. On the server side we enforce quotas; we can configure burst buffers for Dedicated to absorb short spikes. For Hosted there are fair-use limits and quota enforcement that will return 429s if you exceed.
[05:18] Priya Sharma: We want to run a small POC with a couple payment verification flows and an embeddings pipeline for search. How long to stand up Dedicated or Private for a POC?

[05:27] Maya Chen: Dedicated can be provisioned in days once the contract's in place; for a proof-of-concept we often run on Hosted with a reserved test pool so you can benchmark quickly - then move to Dedicated if tail latency and throughput justify it. Private takes longer because of networking and control plane setup - usually weeks.
[05:42] Lena Rodriguez: Cost is a big factor. Can you provide example unit economics: per-token cost differences between Hosted and Dedicated?

[05:48] Maya Chen: We'll send a sample pricing sheet. Generally Dedicated lowers per-token cost for steady high throughput; Hosted is good for bursty or trial usage. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings to further cut costs.
[06:02] Tom Wei: On the LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, do you support streaming embeddings and async calls?

[06:08] Arjun Patel: Yes - streaming for chat, async for embeddings. Our Python SDK integrates with LangChain's async abstractions; LlamaIndex examples show how to swap our client in. I'll share code snippets.
[06:22] Priya Sharma: Any gotchas for model pinning and rollouts? We want safe rollouts when upgrading model versions used in scoring.
[06:28] Maya Chen: Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin routes to a model version and stage traffic gradually while comparing metrics.
[06:40] Lena Rodriguez: For our compliance folks - data retention and deletion controls - can we configure retention windows per environment?

[06:46] Maya Chen: Yes, retention policies are configurable. For Hosted you'd choose retention windows; Dedicated/Private gives greater controls including customer-managed logs and the ability to disable logging to object store.
[06:58] Tom Wei: Let's talk bench - what would you need from us to run a quick benchmark?

[07:03] Arjun Patel: A representative traffic sample CSV is ideal: timestamps, route, payload size, and expected concurrency. Also a list of critical routes with p95/p99 targets. We can run a 48-hour bench but usually a focused spike test plus some sustained load is enough.
[07:18] Priya Sharma: We'll extract a week of anonymized traffic and send it. We also want to test prefix caching impact - many of our templates repeat the same header text.
[07:26] Arjun Patel: Good - we'll include a caching baseline test and show token-cost delta with caching enabled.

[07:34] Maya Chen: Recap and next steps: Arjun will send LangChain/LlamaIndex integration examples and a short gateway sidecar pattern doc; I'll send pricing, Dedicated capacity deck, and SOC2/security pack. Lena will share traffic patterns and SLOs. Proposed follow-up: technical deep-dive (60 min) with your SREs next week. Does that work?
[07:53] Lena Rodriguez: Yes that timeline works. Tom and Priya are in for the deep-dive.
[07:58] Tom Wei: Quick question - for Dedicated SLAs, what's the uptime commitment?
[08:03] Maya Chen: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated; exact numbers depend on the contract tier - we'll include the SLA language in the deck.
[08:14] Priya Sharma: Also, is there a sandbox that supports streaming so we can integrate end-to-end before committing?
[08:20] Arjun Patel: Yes, we provide sandbox keys with streaming enabled and a sample LangChain notebook that demonstrates streaming responses and reconnect logic.
[08:30] Lena Rodriguez: Great. Anything else we should know?

[08:33] Maya Chen: One small gotcha: if you plan to run on-prem private with GPU quantized runtimes, we'll need to match CUDA and kernel versions - Arjun will capture that in the private deployment checklist.
[08:45] Arjun Patel: I'll add the kernel/CUDA checklist to the repo. Also I'll include recommended quantization profiles based on payloads you send.
[08:55] Lena Rodriguez: Perfect. Thank you both. We'll look for the materials and get the traffic sample over by Thursday.
[09:02] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive. Appreciate the time.
[09:08] (call ends)
Notes: minor transcription errors present; some proper nouns (model names) may be misrecognized in places.
